about: The epistola of the formulary “Sexagesima Sunday” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: You gladly put up with the foolish, being wise yourselves. For you bear it if anyone reduces you to slavery, if anyone devours you, if anyone takes from you, if anyone exalts himself, if anyone strikes you in the face. I speak with regard to dishonor, as if we were weak in this matter. In whatever anyone dares — I speak in foolishness — I dare too. They are Hebrews; I am too. They are Israelites; I am too. They are the seed of Abraham; I am too. They are ministers of Christ — speaking as a less wise man — I am more so: in very many labors, in prisons more abundantly, in blows beyond measure, in deaths often. Five times I received from the Jews forty blows less one. Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked, I spent a night and a day in the depths of the sea; in journeys often, in dangers from rivers, dangers from robbers, dangers from my own race, dangers from the Gentiles, dangers in the city, dangers in the wilderness, dangers at sea, dangers among false brethren; in toil and hardship, in many night watches, in hunger and thirst, in frequent fasts, in cold and nakedness; apart from what comes from outside, there is what presses on me daily, the anxious concern for all the churches. Who grows weak, and I do not grow weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn? If I have to glory, my glorying will be in what belongs to my weakness. The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed forever, knows that I am not lying. In Damascus the governor of the nation of King Aretas was guarding the city of the Damascenes in order to seize me, and I was lowered in a basket through a window, down the wall, and so I escaped out of his hands. If I have to glory, it is not profitable, to be sure, but I will come to the Lord’s visions and revelations. I know of a man in Christ; fourteen years ago — whether it was in the body I do not know, or outside the body I do not know, God knows — such a one was caught up as far as the third heaven. I also know of such a man — whether it was in the body or outside the body I do not know, God knows — that he was caught up into paradise and heard hidden words, which a man is not permitted to speak. On behalf of one like this I will glory, but on my own behalf I will not glory in anything except my weaknesses. For even if I wish to glory, I will not be a fool, for I will tell the truth; but I refrain, lest anyone should think of me beyond what he sees in me, or whatever he hears from me. And so that the magnitude of the revelations might not exalt me, I was given a goad of my flesh, an angel of Satan, to strike me. About this I asked the Lord three times that it might leave me, and He said to me: My grace is enough for you, for power is perfected in weakness. Gladly, therefore, I will glory in my weaknesses, so that Christ’s power may dwell in me.
